// structs: composite literals, T{} and &T{}, keyed and positional
// elements, nested literals, and field writes on the result.
u := url.URL{Scheme: "https", Host: "example.com", Path: "/a"};
assert.Equal(tb, "https", u.Scheme);
assert.Equal(tb, "/a", u.Path);

p := &url.URL{Scheme: "https", Host: "h", Path: "/p"};
assert.Equal(tb, "https://h/p", p.String());

// Positional elements fill the fields in declaration order.
s := url.URL{"https"};
assert.Equal(tb, "https", s.Scheme);

// Nested literals, a call as an element, and a numeric literal
// converting to its field's width.
r := &http.Request{Method: "POST", URL: &url.URL{Path: "/n"}, ProtoMajor: 1};
assert.Equal(tb, "POST", r.Method);
assert.Equal(tb, "/n", r.URL.Path);
assert.Equal(tb, "int", fmt.Sprintf("%T", r.ProtoMajor));

c := &http.Request{URL: url.Parse("https://h/c")};
assert.Equal(tb, "/c", c.URL.Path);

// The value a literal builds is addressable, so its fields assign.
w := url.URL{};
w.Path = "/w";
assert.Equal(tb, "/w", w.Path);

// A literal in argument position, and the trailing comma form.
assert.Equal(tb, "/arg", fmt.Sprint(&url.URL{Path: "/arg"}));

m := &url.URL{
	Scheme: "https",
	Host:   "h",
	Path:   "/m",
};
assert.Equal(tb, "https://h/m", m.String());
